primitives.name: Approximate Nonparametric Maximum Likelihood Estimator
primitives.verbatim_quote: Method / model - Approximate NPMLE: replace Ĝ = argmin_{G∈G_T} l(G) (infinite-dim, convex) with Ĝ_Λ = argmin_{G∈G_Λ} l(G) on a finite grid Λ={t_1..t_q}, equivalent to the convex simplex problem min_{w∈Δ^{q-1}} -(1/p)Σ_j log{Σ_k f_0(X_j|t_k) w_k}.

primitives.assumptions: Observations follow mixture model; likelihood kernel is elliptical unimodal; grid covers convex hull of MLEs.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core idea of approximate nonparametric maximum likelihood estimation (NPMLE) involves replacing infinite-dimensional distributions with finite-grid approximations. This allows for convex optimization over a discrete set of parameters, transforming complex integral likelihoods into tractable minimization problems. The key insight is that for elliptical unimodal likelihoods, the true support lies within the convex hull of individual MLEs, making grid-based approximation valid. In GSI, this translates to constructing empirical Bayes posteriors over noisy player/team latent variables, avoiding restrictive parametric assumptions. For GSE, it supports dynamic updating of per-unit states through posterior averaging under learned population priors. The method's robustness to grid density ensures stable inference even with coarse discretization. Dualities arise in how the same optimization framework can be applied to different domains—e.g., baseball batting averages, microarray gene expression, and continuous glucose monitoring—each requiring tailored likelihood kernels but sharing the same computational machinery.
